p.seg: In ancient times, Emperor Yáo,
with his intelligence, wisdom, and thoughtfulness,
shone throughout the world.
When he was about to abdicate his throne,
he yielded it to Yú Shùn,
and thus the "Canon of Yáo" was composed.
Examining antiquity,
it is said:
Emperor Yáo was called Fàngxūn.
He was refined, thoughtful, and composed,
sincerely respectful and capable of yielding.
His light reached the four extremities,
extending to heaven and earth.
He was able to illuminate lofty virtue,
thereby bringing the nine clans close;
once the nine clans were harmonious,
he distinguished and made illustrious
the hundred surnames,
harmonizing the myriad states.
The common people were transformed and prosperous,
and all was peaceful.
He then commanded Xī and Hé,
reverently following the vast heavens;
observing the movements of the sun, moon, and stars,
he respectfully taught the people the seasons.
He separately commanded Xī Zhòng,
to reside at Yúyí,
called Yánggǔ.
There, he reverently welcomed the rising sun,
and regulated the eastern works.
At the equinox, with the star Niǎo,
he determined the mid-spring.
The people then dispersed;
birds and beasts mated and bred.
He further commanded Xī Shū,
to reside in the south, called Dàjiāo.
He regulated the southern transformations.
Reverently, he attended to his duties.
At the solstice, with the star Huǒ,
he determined the mid-summer.
The people then dwelt in high places;
birds and beasts shed their feathers.
He separately commanded Hé Zhòng, to reside in the west,
called Mèigǔ.
There, he reverently bade farewell to the setting sun,
and regulated the western harvest.
At the equinox, with the star Xū,
he determined the mid-autumn.
The people then felt at ease;
birds and beasts grew new fur.
He further commanded Hé Shū,
to reside in the north,
called Yōudū.
He regulated the northern changes.
At the solstice, with the star Mǎo,
he determined the mid-winter.
The people then kept indoors;
birds and beasts grew thick down.
The Emperor said:
"Ah! You, Xī and Hé.
The year is three hundred and sixty-six days,
and by intercalary months
the four seasons are fixed, completing the year.
Thus, the hundred tasks are properly ordered,
and all achievements flourish."
The Emperor said:
"Who is capable of succeeding me and ascending the throne?"
Fàng Qí said:
"Your son Zhū is enlightened."
The Emperor said: "Alas! He is quarrelsome and contentious;
can he do?"
The Emperor said:
"Who is capable of assisting me in governance?"
Huān Dōu said:
"Ah! Gōnggōng has everywhere accomplished works."
The Emperor said:
"Alas! His words are fair but his actions contrary,
and he appears respectful while overflowing with pride."
The Emperor said:
"Ah! Four Chiefs,
the vast flood waters are causing devastation,
encircling the hills and overwhelming the heights,
so mighty they reach the heavens;
the people below are lamenting.
Is there anyone who can control it?"
All said:
"Oh! Gǔn!"
The Emperor said:
"Alas! He is disobedient! He disobeys orders
and ruins his clan."
The Chiefs said:
"We think otherwise.
Let him try, and if he can, then proceed."
The Emperor said:
"Go, and be reverent!"
After nine years,
the work had not been accomplished.
The Emperor said:
"Ah! Four Chiefs.
I have been on the throne for seventy years;
you can carry out the mandate,
and succeed to my throne."
The Chiefs said: "We lack virtue and would disgrace the imperial throne."
It was said:
"Display the wise and promote the obscure."
Regarding the imperial throne, it was said:
"Display the wise and promote the obscure."
All advised the Emperor, saying:
"There is a solitary man below,
named Yú Shùn."
The Emperor said:
"Yes! I have heard of him.
What is he like?"
The Chiefs said:
"He is the son of a blind man;
his father is obstinate,
his mother is insincere,
and his brother Xiàng is arrogant.
Yet he has been able to harmonize
with filial piety, so that his family is gradually well-ordered,
and he does not fall into evil."
The Emperor said:
"I will test him!"
He gave him his daughters in marriage,
to observe his behavior through the two women.
He sent down the two women to Guīruì,
to be wives to Yú.
The Emperor said:
"Be reverent!"
Yú Shùn was of lowly origin.
Yáo heard of his intelligence and wisdom.
He intended to have him succeed to the throne.
He tested him through various difficulties.
Thus, the "Canon of Shùn" was composed.
Examining antiquity, Emperor Shùn,
called Chónghuá, was in harmony with the Emperor.
He was profound, wise, civilized, and enlightened,
gentle, respectful, sincere, and solid.
His hidden virtue rose to be heard,
and he was commanded to take the position.
He carefully set forth the five teachings,
and the five teachings were followed.
He was placed in charge of all affairs,
and all affairs were orderly.
He received guests at the four gates,
and the four gates were reverent.
He was sent into the great wilderness,
where fierce winds, thunder, and rain did not lead him astray.
The Emperor said:
"Come, you Shùn!
I have inquired into your affairs and examined your words,
and your words have led to achievements,
over three years;
you shall ascend the imperial throne."
Shùn yielded to one of greater virtue
and did not succeed.
On the first auspicious day of the first month,
he received the completion of duties at the Temple of the Cultured Ancestor.
He observed the jade spheres and the jade tube,
to harmonize the seven governors.
Then he sacrificed to the Supreme Deity,
offered to the six honored ones,
worshiped the mountains and rivers,
and paid homage to all the spirits.
He collected the five tokens of jade;
after the month, he chose a day,
to receive the four chiefs and all the rulers,
and returned the jade tokens to the various lords.
In the second month of the year,
he made a tour of inspection to the east,
arriving at Dàizōng,
where he offered a burnt sacrifice;
and worshiped the mountains and rivers in order.
Thereafter, he received the eastern lords.
He harmonized the seasons and months, fixed the days;
unified the pitch-pipes, measures, weights, and scales.
He regulated the five ceremonies,
the five kinds of jade,
the three kinds of silk,
the two living animals,
and the one dead animal
as presents;
as for the five instruments,
they were returned after the ceremonies.
In the fifth month,
he made a tour of inspection to the south,
arriving at the Southern Mountain,
with the same ceremonies as at Dàizōng.
In the eighth month,
he made a tour of inspection to the west,
arriving at the Western Mountain,
with the same ceremonies as before.
In the eleventh month,
he made an inspection tour to the north,
arriving at the Northern Peak,
following the same rituals as at the Western Peak.
Upon returning,
he offered sacrifices to the Ancestral Temple,
using a single bull.
Every five years, he made one inspection tour,
and the feudal lords paid him court visits four times;
they reported in words,
their merits were clearly tested,
and they were rewarded with chariots and robes according to their services.
He established twelve provinces,
erected altars on twelve mountains,
and deepened the rivers.
He instituted the regular punishments.
Banishment was used as a mitigation of the five punishments.
The whip was employed in official punishments,
the rod in educational punishments,
and fines could be paid for redeemable punishments.
For unintentional offenses and those caused by misfortune, pardon was granted;
for those who persisted in evil and were recalcitrant, punishment was inflicted.
Be reverent, be reverent,
and be compassionate in the use of punishments!
He banished Gōnggōng to Yōuzhōu,
exiled Huāndōu to Chóngshān,
drove the Sānmíáo to Sānwēi,
and confined Gǔn to Yǔshān;
after these four criminals were punished, all under Heaven submitted.
In the twenty-eighth year,
the Emperor passed away.
The people felt as if they had lost their own parents;
for three years,
throughout the four seas, the eight kinds of music were silenced.
On the first day of the first month,
Shùn went to the temple of the Cultured Ancestor.
He consulted with the Four Peaks,
opened the four gates,
clarified his vision in all directions,
and made his hearing reach to the four corners.
He inquired of the twelve pastors,
saying:
"Food is essential,
and it must be timely! Be gentle to the distant and kind to the near,
honor virtue and trust the good,
and keep at a distance the artful-tongued,
so that the barbarous tribes may all submit."
Shùn said:
"Ah! Four Peaks.
Is there anyone who can diligently
expand the Emperor's affairs,
to occupy the office of Prime Minister,
and brilliantly assist in managing the various departments?"
They all said:
"There is Bó Yǔ, who is Minister of Works."
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Ah, Yǔ,
you have regulated the waters and the land;
now, be diligent in this!"
Yǔ bowed his head to the ground,
and declined in favor of Jì, Qì, and Gāo Yáo.
The Emperor said:
"Yes!
But you must go!"
The Emperor said:
"Jì! The black-haired people are suffering from famine.
You, as Minister of Agriculture,
must sow the various grains in their seasons."
The Emperor said:
"Qì! The people are not affectionate,
and the five relationships are not harmonious.
You shall be Minister of Education,
reverently spread the five teachings,
with gentleness."
The Emperor said:
"Gāo Yáo! The barbarous tribes disturb our Xià,
committing robberies and villainies.
You shall be Minister of Crime,
the five punishments have their appropriate applications,
and the five applications are to be carried out in three places;
the five banishments have their assigned abodes,
and the five abodes are in three remote regions.
Only through intelligence can justice be achieved."
The Emperor said:
"Who will regulate my various artisans?"
They all said:
"There is Chuí!"
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Ah, Chuí.
You shall be Minister of Works."
Chuí bowed his head to the ground,
and declined in favor of Shū, Qiāng and Bó Yǔ.
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Go,
and you will harmonize."
The Emperor said:
"Who will regulate for me the grasses, trees, birds, and beasts?"
They all said:
"There is Yì!"
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Ah, Yì,
you shall be my Forester."
Yì bowed his head to the ground,
and declined in favor of Zhū, Hǔ, Xióng, and Pí.
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Go, and you will harmonize."
The Emperor said:
"Ah! Four Peaks.
Is there anyone who can direct my three ceremonies?"
They all said:
"There is Bó Yí."
The Emperor said:
"Yes! Ah, Bó.
You shall be Minister of Religious Ceremonies.
Morning and night be reverent,
upright and pure."
Bó bowed his head to the ground,
and declined in favor of Kuí and Lóng.
The Emperor said:
"Yes. Go, be reverent!"
The Emperor said:
"Kuí!
I appoint you to be Minister of Music,
and to teach the youth.
Make them straightforward yet gentle,
broad-minded yet dignified,
strong but not brutal,
simple but not arrogant.
Poetry is the expression of earnest thought;
singing is the prolonged utterance of that expression;
the notes accompany that utterance,
and they are harmonized by the pitch-pipes.
In this way the eight kinds of instruments can be adjusted so that
one shall not take the place of another,
and spirits and men are brought into harmony."
Kuí said:
"Oh! I strike the stone, I tap the stone,
and the various animals lead one another to dance."
The Emperor said:
"Lóng! I detest slanderous speakers and destroyers of virtue,
who agitate and alarm my people.
I appoint you to be Minister of Communication.
Morning and night you shall issue my orders and report to me,
being always truthful."
The Emperor said:
"Ah! You twenty-two men,
be reverent! So shall you assist in the service of Heaven."
Every three years there was an examination of merits;
after three examinations,
there were degradations and promotions, and the unenlightened and enlightened were distinguished.
Thus all the duties were successfully performed.
The Sānmíáo were segregated according to their tribes.
Shùn was thirty years of age when he was called to employment;
he served for thirty years;
he was on the throne for fifty years, and then he died on a journey to the south.
The Emperor regulated the lands below,
and set up the residences according to the regions,
distinguishing the people by their clans and classes,
he composed the "Gǔ Zuò"
and the nine pieces of "Jiǔ Gòng".
the "Gǎo Yù".
Gāo Yáo laid out his plans,
Yǔ completed his labors,
and Emperor Shùn celebrated them.
Thus were made the "Dà Yǔ", the "Gāo Yáo Mó",
and the "Yì Jì".
"Examining into antiquity,"
we find that Dà Yǔ,
named Wén Mìng, spread his influence throughout the four seas,
and reverently received the favor of the Emperor.
He said,
"If the sovereign can realize the difficulty of being a sovereign,
and the minister the difficulty of being a minister,
government will be well-ordered,
and the people will be stimulated to virtue."
The Emperor said:
"Yes!
If indeed such be the case,
good words will not be hidden.
No men of virtue and talents will be left neglected in the country,
and all the states will enjoy peace."
He examined the views of the multitude,
"giving up his own opinion to follow that of others,"
"not oppressing the helpless,
nor neglecting the straitened."
It was only the Emperor who could attain to this.
Yì said:
"Oh!
The Emperor's virtue is vast and far-reaching;
he is sage, spiritual,
martial, and accomplished."
Heaven regarded him with favor and appointed him,
so that he became sovereign of all within the four seas as the ruler of the world.
Yǔ said:
"To follow the path of reason is fortunate;
to follow reverse courses is unlucky,
as shadow follows substance."
Yì said:
"Alas!
Be cautious!
Be watchful when there is no cause for alarm,
do not lose the laws and regulations,
do not indulge in idleness,
do not indulge in pleasures.
'Appoint the virtuous without hesitation,
remove the wicked without doubt.'
Do not carry out doubtful plans,
and all your intentions will be bright.
Do not violate the Way to seek the praise of the people,
do not oppose the people to follow your own desires.
Be neither negligent nor extravagant,
and the four barbarians will come to acknowledge your sovereignty."
Yǔ said:
"Oh!
Let the Emperor keep this in mind.
Virtue lies in good governance,
and governance lies in nurturing the people.
'Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain—
these must be regulated;
correcting virtue, utilizing resources, and enriching life—
these must be harmonized.'
When the nine achievements are in order,
the nine orders are sung.
'Admonish with goodness,
oversee with authority,
encourage with the nine songs,
so that they do not deteriorate.'"
The Emperor said:
"Yes!
'The land is leveled and heaven’s work is accomplished.'
The six treasuries and three affairs are truly well managed,
and for ten thousand generations, they will rely on this—
this is your achievement."
The Emperor said:
"Come,
you, Yǔ!
I have resided on the imperial throne for thirty-three years;
in my old age, I am weary of toil.
You are untiring,
take command of my multitudes."
Yǔ said:
"My virtue is insufficient,
the people will not rely on me.
'Gāo Yáo diligently sowed virtue,
and virtue thus descended.'
'The common people cherish him.'
Let the Emperor keep this in mind.
'Think of this in this,
set this aside in this,
speak of this in this,
and sincerely act from this in this.
Only the Emperor contemplates achievements.'"
The Emperor said:
"Gāo Yáo!
'Only these ministers and multitudes'
do not oppose my governance.
'You serve as the minister of justice.'
Be clear about the five punishments,
to assist the five teachings.
Aim for my governance,
punishments aim for no punishments,
and the people abide by the mean.
This is your achievement. Be diligent!"
Gāo Yáo said:
"The Emperor’s virtue is without fault,
he governs the people with simplicity,
and leads the multitudes with leniency;
punishments do not extend to descendants,
rewards extend to future generations;
'pardoning unintended offenses, no matter how great,
punishing intentional crimes, no matter how small.'
When in doubt about a crime, be lenient,
when in doubt about merit, be generous.
'Rather than kill the innocent,
it is better to err on the side of irregularity.'
The virtue of cherishing life
resonates with the people’s hearts.
Thus, they do not offend against the authorities."
The Emperor said:
"'You enable me to follow my desires in governance.'
The four quarters respond like the wind,
this is your excellence."
The Emperor said:
"Come!
Yǔ."
"'The Floodwaters warned me.'
'You achieved what you promised and accomplished the task.'
Only you are worthy,
diligent in serving the state,
frugal in managing your household,
without self-satisfaction or pretension.
Only you are worthy,
'You do not boast,
so no one in the world can contend with your abilities.'
You do not boast of your achievements,
so no one in the world can contend with your merits.
I praise your virtue,
and commend your great achievements.
'Heaven’s mandate rests upon your person.'
You shall eventually ascend to the great throne.
'The human mind is precarious,
the moral mind is subtle.'
Be refined and single-minded,
'sincerely hold fast to the mean.'
Do not listen to unverified words,
do not employ unconsulted plans.
Is it not the sovereign who should be loved?
Is it not the people who should be feared?
'Without a great sovereign,
whom would the multitudes look up to?
Without the multitudes,
the sovereign has none to guard the state.'
Be reverent!
'Be cautious in your position.'
Respectfully cultivate what is desirable.
'If all within the four seas are in distress and poverty,
Heaven’s favor will end forever.'
'From the mouth come both good and war.'
My words will not be repeated."
Yǔ said:
"Let us cast lots among the meritorious ministers,
and follow the auspicious one."
The Emperor said:
"Yǔ!
'In official divination, the will is first determined,
then the great tortoise is consulted.'
My will is already fixed,
consultations and plans are all in agreement,
the spirits and gods approve,
the tortoise and milfoil concur,
'the divination does not repeatedly show auspiciousness.'"
Yǔ bowed and touched his head to the ground
firmly declining.
The Emperor said:
"Do not!
Only you are suitable."
On the first day of the first month, at dawn,
he received the mandate at the Shénzōng temple;
leading the hundred officials, as the Emperor had done at the beginning.
The Emperor said:
"Alas,
Yǔ!
Now the Yǒumiáo are not submitting,
you go and campaign!"
Yǔ then assembled the lords,
and addressed the army, saying:
"O numerous hosts,
all listen to my command.
These foolish Yǒumiáo,
are deluded and disrespectful,
arrogant and self-righteous,
opposing the Way and corrupting virtue.
'The noble are in obscurity,
the petty are in positions.'
The people are abandoned and unprotected,
Heaven has sent down calamity upon them.
Therefore, I lead you, my multitude of officers,
'to uphold justice and punish the guilty.'
May you unite your hearts and strength,
and surely achieve merit."
After thirty days,
the Miáo people defied the command.
Yì advised Yǔ, saying:
"Only virtue moves Heaven,
there is no distance it cannot reach.
Pride brings loss,
humility receives benefit—
this is the Way of Heaven.
When the Emperor was at Lìshān,
'he went to the fields,
daily crying out to the compassionate Heaven
and to his parents.'
Bearing guilt and acknowledging fault,
'he reverently attended to Gǔsǒu,
trembling with awe and caution.
Gǔsǒu also became truly agreeable.'
Sincerity moves the spirits,
how much more these Yǒumiáo?"
"Yǔ bowed and praised these words, saying:
'Yes!'"
He withdrew the army and restored order.
The Emperor then extensively displayed civil virtue,
dancing with shields and feathers between the two staircases.
After seventy days, the Yǒumiáo submitted.
Examining antiquity, Gāo Yáo said:
"'Truly practice his virtue,
and plans will be enlightened and assistance harmonious.'"
Yǔ said:
"'Yes! But how?'"
Gāo Yáo said:
"Ah! Be cautious in cultivating your personal
conduct, and think of lasting ways.
Sincerely order the nine classes of kindred,
and the many wise will encourage and assist;
from near, it can extend far—
this lies herein."
Yǔ bowed in acknowledgment of these good words,
saying: "Yes!"
Gāo Yáo said:
"Ah! It lies in knowing people,
and in tranquilizing the people."
Yǔ said:
"Alas! All being so,
even the Emperor finds it difficult.
To know people is wisdom,
enabling one to appoint men to office;
to tranquilize the people is kindness,
and the black-haired people will cherish it.
If one can be both wise and kind,
why worry about Huān Dōu?
Why banish the Yǒu Miáo?
Why fear those of artful speech,
insinuating appearance, and great wickedness?"
Gāo Yáo said:
"Ah! There are also nine virtues to be practiced.
When we say of a man that he has virtue,
we say:
He follows this with specific actions."
Yǔ said:
"What are they?"
Gāo Yáo said:
"Affable yet grave,
mild yet firm,
sincere yet respectful,
capable yet cautious,
docile yet bold,
straightforward yet gentle,
simple yet honest,
strong yet just,
courageous yet righteous;
displaying these constantly,
auspicious indeed!
He who daily manifests three virtues,
early and late cultivating and illustrating them, may have a family.
He who daily respects and reverently practices six virtues,
may brighten his services and have a state.
When all are received and widely employed,
the nine virtues all being engaged,
the talented and virtuous are in office,
all officers emulate one another,
and all craftsmen are timely in their work;
harmonizing with the five elements,
all achievements are consolidated.
Do not let those who have states indulge in ease and desire,
but be cautious and diligent,
for in one day, two days, there are myriad crises.
Do not leave offices vacant,
for Heaven's work must be carried out by men.
Heaven has arranged its codes,
ordaining us to make the five bonds ever more sincere!
Heaven has its orders of rank,
from us the five ceremonies
have their constant use!
Let us be united in reverence and respect,
and harmonious in heart!
Heaven appoints the virtuous,
with the five robes and their five distinctions!
Heaven punishes the guilty,
with the five punishments and their five applications!
Be diligent in government affairs! Be diligent!
Heaven's hearing and vision
come from our people's hearing and vision;
Heaven's enlightenment and awe
come from our people's enlightenment and awe.
Penetrating above and below,
be reverent, you who possess the land!"
Gāo Yáo said:
"My words are in accordance with reason,
and can be carried into practice."
Yǔ said:
"Yes!
Your words may lead to achievements."
Gāo Yáo said:
"I have no knowledge to think of,
but I wish to assist in your efforts."
The Emperor said:
"Come! Yǔ, you too must speak good words."
Yǔ bowed and said:
"Ah! Emperor, what should I say?
I think only of daily diligence."
Gāo Yáo said:
"Alas! How so?"
Yǔ said:
"The flood waters rose to the heavens,
vast and mighty, encircling the mountains and overwhelming the hills;
the people below were bewildered and submerged.
I traveled in four conveyances,
and along the mountains hewed wood.
Together with Yì, I presented fresh game to the multitude.
I opened the nine rivers,
leading them to the four seas;
deepened the channels and ditches,
leading them to the streams.
Together with Jì, I sowed and presented to the multitude difficult-to-obtain food and fresh provisions,
facilitating exchange
to circulate goods and dwellings.
Then the people were able to sustain themselves,
and all regions began to be governed."
Gāo Yáo said:
"Yes! We should follow your good words."
Yǔ said:
"Ah! Emperor, be cautious in your position."
The Emperor said:
"Yes!"
Yǔ said:
"Be calm in your stopping,
attentive to the subtle and the tranquil;
assist with uprightness,
and every movement will be greatly responded to.
Await the will to be clearly received from God,
and Heaven will renew its mandate with favor."
The Emperor said:
"Alas! Ministers are like neighbors!
Neighbors are like ministers!"
Yǔ said:
"Yes!"
The Emperor said:
"Ministers are my limbs, ears, and eyes.
I wish to aid and govern the people,
and you assist me;
I wish to exert strength in all directions,
and you act for me;
I wish to see the symbols of the ancients,
the sun, moon, stars, and constellations,
mountains, dragons, and the flowery fowl,
depicted on the ceremonial robes, the ancestral temple vessels,
water plants, fire, grain,
axes, and the distinction figures, embroidered on silken fabrics,
with the five colors displayed in the five hues,
to make robes,
and you make them clear;
I wish to hear the six pitch-pipes,
the five tones, and the eight sounds,
to examine governance and neglect,
and to bring forth and receive the five statements,
and you listen for me;
when I err,
you correct me;
do not follow me to my face,
and behind my back have contrary words.
Respect the four assistants;
if the multitude is stubborn and slanderous,
and does not follow this,
use the target to make it clear to them,
and the whip to remind them;
write it down to record it,
wishing they may still live together.
Officers should receive words,
and when timely, promulgate them;
if they reform, receive and employ them;
if not, punish them."
Yǔ said:
"Yes indeed! Emperor.
Throughout the brilliant heavens,
to the corners of the sea,
the multitude of living beings,
and the worthy among the black-haired people of all regions
are all your subjects.
May the Emperor constantly promote them,
broadly receiving their words,
clearly examining them by their merits,
and rewarding them with carriages and robes according to their services.
Who would dare not be humble?
Who would dare not respectfully respond?
If the Emperor does not do so timely,
promoting all alike, daily efforts will be without merit.
Do not be like Dān Zhū, who was arrogant,
fond only of idleness and pleasure,
indulging in pride and cruelty,
without cease day and night; he boated on dry land.
He engaged in wantonness at home;
thus his lineage was cut off.
I took warning from this,
marrying a woman of Túshān,
and in the days Xīn, Rén, Guǐ, and Jiǎ;
when Qǐ cried 'gū-gū,'
I did not cherish him,
